time.desc: The university involved issued a response to the public opinion triggered by the first-instance judgment of the library dispute, stating that it would conduct an investigation and review of key issues such as student punishment and dissertations.

The content platform issued a disposal announcement and confirmed that a user had impersonated the identity related to the incident and spread false information, and then permanently banned the relevant account.
The parties involved in the dispute publicly released self-defense materials in response to their dissertation issues and related accusations, further triggering a backlash from public opinion.
A third party related to the incident filed a lawsuit against the university involved, and the dispute entered a new stage of legal action with clear civil procedures for the first time.
A case involving a dispute involving a university library was confirmed to enter the second instance procedure, and the appeal was accepted by the court
The master's degree thesis related to the university involved was removed from the academic literature platform, raising concerns about the source and procedure of retraction.
The court of second instance made the final judgment and upheld the original judgment, rejecting all the plaintiff's appeals, and the substantive disputes in the case became a judicial finality.

The university involved issued a notice: revoking the disciplinary sanctions against the accused students and announcing the conclusion of the thesis review. At the same time, relevant responsible personnel will be held accountable.

The parties involved in the dispute once again spoke out intensively on social platforms to defend themselves and had verbal conflicts with others, triggering a new round of public opinion fluctuations.

The party involved in the dispute posted and quickly denied the statement related to the public service examination on social platforms, which was criticized by public opinion as false information and topic hype.
Blogger exposed the accuser's falsification of test transcripts and academic integrity issues in past award-winning papers
A judgment document circulating on the Internet was found to have been artificially deleted with key drug purchase record paragraphs, and the authenticity of the document was questioned.
Platform posts allege that there are organized accounts that continue to clear ground for the accuser and discredit the accused, implying manipulation of public opinion.
Mainstream media published comments criticizing the universities involved for using excuses to wait for superiors and refusing to promptly correct and punish them.
A blogger's article supporting the accuser was blocked and removed from the platform a few hours after it was published. The blogger said he was besieged by organized reports.
Several high school classmates and alumni of the accused party provided real-name materials to reporters to prove their history of misconduct in high school.
Media reported that a large number of brotherly aid accounts have emerged on social platforms to teach men strategies for dealing with sexual harassment accusations and even violent confrontations.
The main person in charge of the party committee of the university involved was replaced. The arrival of the new person in charge was closely connected with the subsequent error correction report.

The announcements from the universities involved showed that each of them had fifty major objections, triggering further public doubts about the zero cost of false accusations and the attribution of responsibility.
Another university (Institution B) officially revoked Person B’s doctoral admission qualification and removed him from the list of proposed doctoral students.

Institution B issued a public clarification on the doctoral application rumors, stating that it had never accepted or processed Person B's doctoral application, and that previous reports that it had "removed the list of candidates for admission" were untrue.
After losing the first instance, Character B was accused of continuing to incite online violence and threatening and harassing the judge presiding over the case.

It was revealed that Organization K hid the disciplinary documents against Person A on the school network and was only accessible through the school IP. This was interpreted by the outside world as a wait-and-see strategy waiting for the final judicial review.
In addition to Character B’s dissertation being removed from the shelves, his mentor’s related articles have also been withdrawn.

Organization K announced the accountability of relevant responsible persons in the notification, including suspending the enrollment qualifications of the tutors involved for two years and giving relevant managers intra-party warnings or admonishments.
Organization K clarified in the report that the rumor that "Character B's uncle holds the title A in the school" is not true

Institution K issued a more detailed review description, saying that an investigation team composed of five experts investigated 21 people and reviewed 91 pieces of evidence. It determined that Person B’s dissertation was not plagiarized and the degree would not be revoked.
